newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to levy sales tax on multimedia computers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to levy sales tax on multimedia computers.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry on Wednesday said it might impose a new sales tax on multimedia computers.

"According to taxation rules, multimedia computers should be imposed with a sales tax of 10-13 percent if they are sold along with such standard outfits as CDROMs and speakers," Lin Yung-tse, a deputy dirctor of the ministry's taxation department, told Reuters.
Currently, stereo sets are levied with a 10-percent sales tax and video recorders and television sets a 13-percent sales tax. Computers, however, are free from such tax, Lin said.

The local Economic Daily News reported on Wednesday that if multimedia computers are hit with a sales tax, computer makers' profits would be cut and the retail price of multimedia computers would soar.

The paper quoted an industrial source as saying if the government insists on imposing sales tax on multimedia computers, the tax should be levied only on the CDROM and the speaker instead of the computer itself.
Another economic official said the ministry's national tax agencies have contacted several local multimedia computer makers to assess their reaction.
"If their computers' original design does not include the CDROMs and speakers, and it is the user who assembles (it), then the system will not be taxed, he said.
